profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC4 sits at 22210 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus. Unlike most of the other LC-numbered buildings, LC4 is individually and specifically named on CloudHQ's current LC Campus page as one of two buildings, alongside LC3, actively under construction, with the company stating a "Ready for Service within 20 months" timeline for that new capacity as of this session's retrieval. A third-party data center aggregator separately reports 180 megawatts specifically for LC4, a figure this profile notes as unconfirmed by the operator rather than adopting as fact, particularly given CloudHQ's own materials describe this specific building as still under construction rather than fully operational. CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

CloudHQ's "campus within a campus" marketing concept at LC allows customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment, a positioning particularly relevant to LC4 as one of two buildings currently under active construction and leasing, alongside LC3. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing footprint.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC4 is one building within a fourteen-building campus in Ashburn, Virginia that CloudHQ describes as totaling 1,256 MW of critical IT load across 8.5 million square feet, with 756 MW currently available. LC4 itself is under construction with a stated timeline of ready for service within twenty months as of this retrieval, so no operational capacity can yet be assigned to it. A third-party aggregator reports 180 MW for this specific building, but this figure is unconfirmed by the operator and unreliable given the building's incomplete status.

The LC Campus as a whole ranks twenty-fourth among Virginia facilities with published megawatt figures, though this ranking reflects the full fourteen-building campus, not LC4 alone. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities statewide but only 23 with published capacity figures totaling 1,375 MW, meaning the LC Campus represents the vast majority of Virginia's disclosed AI infrastructure footprint. Dominion Energy serves the region but the operator does not name which utility will serve this campus on its current materials.

LC4 matters to AI scaling only as a future asset once construction completes and capacity comes online. Until that point it represents planned supply rather than available compute, and the individual building's capacity specification remains unpublished by the operator.
